items.title: Hollywood falls for Como: Champions League football by the lake
items.summary: Seven years ago they were playing amateur football. Now they are hosting Europe’s biggest clubs. With Cesc Fàbregas, more than €400 million invested and stars in the stands, Como are aiming to become a global brand
items.content:
There is a place in Europe where Champions League football is played just metres from a lake, where vintage wooden Riva water taxis speed across the water and vintage seaplanes come in to land. It is a picture-postcard setting famous around the world, especially since George Clooney bought a holiday home here. And Hollywood stars are increasingly buying tickets to watch Como, a club that was playing amateur football just seven years ago and is now preparing to host Manchester United.

The Lombardy city of 85,000 people, close to the Swiss border, is the setting for one of the most remarkable experiments in European football. After finishing fourth in Serie A last season, Como are playing Champions League football at the Stadio Sinigaglia, upgraded in record time to meet Uefa standards.

At the heart of the project is Catalan coach Cesc Fàbregas, whose team play a fast-passing game built around young talent, almost all of it from abroad, including Nico Paz, Jacobo Ramón and Lucas Da Cunha, recently called up by France.

In 2019, the club had five employees. Today it has 300. Como is owned by Indonesia’s Hartono family, which made its fortune in tobacco and now has interests ranging from banking to property.

Club president Mirwan Suwarso comes from the media world: he produced films and worked in television in London. Como was conceived partly as a story to be told, turning a local limitation into a global advantage.

The stadium holds just 12,370 people, but the lake, its villas and its celebrities are known around the world.

“Our local fan base is limited, but the audience we can engage globally is unlimited,” Suwarso says.

Only a few years ago, almost all online purchases of shirts and merchandise came from the local area. Today, the city and province of Como account for just 14 per cent of customers. London, Paris, Rome, Milan and New York are the leading cities. Alongside football, the club’s channels also feature documentaries about Como and its lake.

“What does the Premier League have that we don’t? Money. But we have history, art, food and passion. And the most beautiful lake in the world,” Suwarso says.

The owners have nevertheless invested more than €400 million over seven years. “Italian football also needs to sell the country around it abroad.”

Como is aiming to become a global luxury brand. Hugh Grant, Keira Knightley, Adrien Brody, Michael Fassbender, Thierry Henry and Arsène Wenger have all been seen at the Sinigaglia.

The Sinigaglia is the symbol of it all: from the stands, spectators can see sailing boats and the arc of the Alps.

For months, it appeared that Champions League football might force Como to play elsewhere. Instead, the stadium was upgraded over the summer to meet Uefa standards.

Qualification has brought another change. After succeeding with an almost entirely foreign squad, the club is now looking for young Italian players, who are needed to meet the competition’s squad requirements.

The Champions League also brings financial constraints: Uefa rules link spending to revenue.

“One match at San Siro, the home of Inter and Milan, generates as much revenue as eight at the Sinigaglia,” Suwarso says.

The future therefore lies with a global audience. But while Como sells the exclusive image of the lake abroad, the club keeps ticket prices affordable for its most passionate local supporters.

“Como belongs to the people of Como. We see ourselves as guests, not owners.”

That is the gamble: using Hollywood to win over the world while remaining firmly rooted in Como.

items.title: Fertitta, Rubio, Columbus Day and the G20: the road to a Meloni-Trump thaw
items.summary: The US ambassador in Rome, a possible face-to-face meeting in Miami and the NIAF gala: what lies behind the White House’s overture
items.content:
ROME-NEW YORK — They are handling the statement with care, as though it were kryptonite or a shard of fleeting euphoria. Donald Trump says: “My relationship with Giorgia Meloni is very good. I’ve always liked her.” But it would be foolish to read too much into a one-line answer, officials at Palazzo Chigi caution. True, efforts to mend relations with the White House have been under way for some time. The ambassadors have been working behind the scenes — more on that shortly. But above all else, the instinct for self-preservation prevails.

Experience has taught them that much. This, after all, is the president who went from describing Meloni as a “young, beautiful woman, a highly respected and very successful leader” to portraying her as a timid and disappointing ally, even invoking a “restraining order” against the Italian “stalker”. So this is not yet a turning point.

The circumstances behind Trump’s remarks suggest as much. On Friday evening, the president was approached before heading to a rally in Alabama. The question came from Iacopo Luzi, an Italian journalist in the White House press pool. It was therefore an off-the-cuff comment, although probably one informed by discussions with his advisers.

A great deal has happened in recent months. A diplomatic “peace movement” swung into action after the US president’s public insults. At its centre is the US ambassador to Italy, Tilman J. Fertitta. Extremely wealthy, powerful and someone Trump listens to. He also has another card to play: he is contributing significantly to the Republicans’ election campaign in Texas and appears to be using that leverage to help repair relations with the country where he represents the United States.

The other mediator is Marco Rubio, the secretary of state regarded as the reasonable face of an unpredictable administration.

But back to the original question: how much weight should be attached to Trump’s statement? The best way to assess it is in the context of what has happened over the past few days. An extraordinary G7 video conference was held last Friday. Trump secured agreement from his allies to release 100 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves, a measure the US president was keen on as he seeks to curb prices ahead of the midterm elections. He got his way by threatening to halt oil exports to US partners.

Trump was so pleased with the outcome that he praised the Italian prime minister — who was among those who backed the move — as well as the other major European leaders. “Europe has been exceptional,” he said.

But there is more. On October 9, the president will host a White House reception to mark Columbus Day: a gesture towards Rome as well as Italian-American voters, and another opportunity to speak warmly of Meloni.

Then, on October 17, the National Italian American Foundation will hold its annual gala in Washington. The bolder among the intermediaries had informally floated the idea of a trip by the prime minister to present her book I Am Giorgia at the event, with a foreword by Donald Trump Jr.

One obstacle, however, made the prospect more than remote: what would happen if the prime minister sought a meeting and failed to get one? Or worse, if she did not even try, effectively snubbing her ally? NIAF is therefore seeking to invite Secretary of State Marco Rubio, not least because of his Italian heritage. If he accepts, Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani is also likely to attend. The book will have to wait for another occasion.

Those weaving the diplomatic web are still at work. The first scheduled opportunity for the two leaders to cross paths had been the United Nations General Assembly in mid-September, but Meloni conspicuously stayed away.

The next potential meeting is on the sidelines of the G20 in Florida in mid-December. To prepare for the year-end gathering, Fabrizio Saggio, Palazzo Chigi’s diplomatic adviser and summit sherpa, flew to Washington two days ago. He was there to discuss energy, the economy and artificial intelligence — and, as ever, to tend relations with the administration. The hope, of course, is that the Miami summit could provide the setting for a face-to-face meeting marking the thaw. They will try.

As for the summit and relations with Trump, Meloni has also recently considered in private whether to keep the door open to the US proposal to invite Putin to the next G20 hosted by the United States, an option Rubio himself raised at a press conference with Lavrov. Such a move would have been welcomed in Washington.

In the end, however, the prime minister opted for caution, in line with other European leaders who cannot accept Moscow’s threats. She will make her position clear closer to the G20, while assessing Russia’s behaviour in the meantime.

One question remains unanswered: is it really in Meloni’s interests to mend relations with Trump just months before Italy’s general election? And can she maintain a balance without being smothered by his embrace?

The thaw does appear to have begun. But what happens after the November 3 midterms, given that the United States could resume its offensive against Iran? Washington and Rome have already fallen out over the issue, with the US accusing Italy of failing to do enough to support Washington’s efforts. It could happen again.

items.title: The right to narcissism: what Dalí can teach today’s influencers
items.summary: “Dalí and Fashion”, at Milan’s Palazzo Reale, shows how the artist refused to be trapped by a ready-made identity, choosing instead to reinvent himself time and again
items.content:
MILAN – Is there such a thing as a right to narcissism? In the age of social media, self-promotion is regarded by much of the intellectual world as improper, vulgar, even abhorrent. Yet despite the ever-growing ranks of improvised “content creators” — artists, writers, cultural commentators, even academics — self-promotion is often accompanied by a sense of guilt, as though it were some terrible mistake: a concession to the times, a surrender to a logic we ought instead to despise.

One antidote to this embarrassment might be Dalí and Fashion , the exhibition at Palazzo Reale in Milan (until January 31, 2027, curated by Laura Bartolomé and Judith Clark, with Montse Aguer as scientific director). Walking through it, I found myself wondering whether Dalí was not only a remarkable forerunner of the cultural influencer, but also a possible answer to the mediocrity of the reluctant influencer: an ancestor who can still show us what it means to meticulously construct an image, to turn one’s public persona into creative material that defies categorisation.

Moving through the paintings, jewellery, clothes, brands, inventions, encounters and collaborations with some of fashion’s defining figures — Elsa Schiaparelli, Coco Chanel, Christian Dior, Paco Rabanne — and, above all, his relationship with Gala Dalí, whose wardrobe occupies a large part of the exhibition, a universe emerges in which everything seems capable of being marked, signed and “initiated” into new forms of existence. Dalí has no fixed “nature”; the only thing fixed about him is change. Transformation is his sole constant.

Today we fear the filters that distort our faces and the deepfakes that multiply our identities. For Dalí, by contrast, masks and disguise were indispensable tools for reshaping his own image — altering it and adapting it to every new context.

And to anyone who objects that Dalí was first and foremost an artist — asserting his superiority over the lower ranks of social-media hucksters, snake-oil salesmen and young influencers busy “promoting themselves” in the hope of carving out a space — it is worth recalling what his friend, the photographer Philippe Halsman, said of him: “Dalí is a surrealist. [...] But the most surreal of all his creations is himself. I don’t know what made him more famous: his paintings or the legend he helped create.”

Advertising pitchman, model, star of promotional films, Dalí was in every sense a man who gave himself over to the marketplace, thoroughly of this world. Long before many others, he understood the need to resist settling into a state of respectable normality and instead to invent his own spectacular persona, his own public phantom: “Very rarely in my life have I demeaned myself by wearing civilian clothes. I always wear the Dalí uniform.”

Year after year, Dalí never ignored the trauma of contact — of contamination — with the world. Instead, he chose to turn every incident into an event, staging and theatricalising his life until it became a succession of public appearances. Dalí himself described this when writing about his move to the United States in the 1940s: “I had to change my skin at all costs, to exchange this worn-out epidermis in which I had dressed, hidden and displayed myself, in which I had struggled, fought and triumphed, for another, new skin: the flesh of my desire, of my imminent rebirth. New country, new skin.”

There is, of course, something profoundly provincial, even childish, about the desire to conquer the centre of the world, to be looked at any cost. An anecdote recounted by Rem Koolhaas in Delirious New York captures this perfectly.

When Dalí arrived in New York, he had a baguette more than seven-foot long made for the occasion. But when he landed in Manhattan, the journalists who rushed to interview him failed to ask a single question about the bizarre object tucked under his arm. The discovery was disconcerting: in Manhattan, surrealism had already become invisible.

Yet here too Dalí gives expression to an impulse that feels distinctly contemporary, echoing an age dominated — at least until the day before yesterday — by selfies and endlessly circulating icons, from the trailblazing genius of Paris Hilton to the latest generation of influencers, increasingly unable to make their mark in a marketplace that relentlessly churns out new images and new, “artificial” faces.

But Dalí had grasped something that remains relevant today: when a single appearance is no longer enough, you have to multiply your alliances, build circles and fashionable courts, create unexpected opportunities for display. It is not so different from what social media can do when it functions as an amplifier, building a network of gazes around an occurrence that makes it visible — that, in effect, invents it as an event.

Laura Whitcomb makes a similar point in her essay for the exhibition catalogue: “Our current context of digital feeds and overlapping social circles appears not as a break with the past, but as a vast, unintended amplification of the Dalinian prototype.”

Speaking by phone, fashion theorist and curator Maria Luisa Frisa tells me of the artist’s extraordinary powers of anticipation: “Salvador Dalí is embedded in the imperfect tense of the avant-garde. Hermaphrodite being. Narcissus. A living work of art like the Marchesa Casati. A visionary genius. Capable of spreading his talent everywhere: prints distributed with mass-market newspapers, bottles of Punt e Mes, lithographs printed by the thousand. And yet pop before Warhol. Off-piste before Cattelan.”

A right to narcissism, then? When Narcissus first sees his own image reflected in the water, he does not recognise himself. Perhaps this is where the myth truly begins: not in self-recognition, but in the astonishment of confronting an image that appears strange.

If the myth of Narcissus has been misunderstood for too long, Dalí suggests that the true narcissist is precisely someone capable of looking at himself as though he were an alien, turning his own image into something mutable, even ecological, because it is radically intermingled with animals, plants, jewellery and clothes — in short, with everything that reaches beyond human centrality.

To love oneself as a mystery, to treat oneself as something one can never fully know: Dalí teaches us not to succumb to an identity that has already been assigned to us, but to choose it, reinvent it and reclaim it time and again, even when it becomes entangled with the marketplace and the necessity of self-promotion.

And he reminds us that the way to resist banality is, ultimately, to make convention tremble: static images, fixed identities, clothes already worn thin, incapable of surprising us or sending a shiver down our spines. Because, as Dalí himself liked to say, our first garment — our first fashion — is nothing other than goosebumps.

(Giorgiomaria Cornelio is a poet, writer, filmmaker and performer.)

items.title: The farming nerd growing 240 varieties of tomato in Puglia — and how they end up as gourmet dishes
items.summary: At Borgo Egnazia, agronomist Angelo Giordano runs the Seed House – a seed bank dedicated to preserving biodiversity. Around 30 of the varieties grown in its gardens have already found their way onto chef Domingo Schingaro’s menu
items.content:
In Puglia, simply asking for a tomato is no longer enough. A Tondino di Ginosa, a Cannellino and a Re Umberto can have very different culinary uses. Some are better suited to sauces, others retain more of their freshness, while still others are ideal for fermentation. Calling them all tomatoes is a shortcut, rather like ordering a glass of wine without caring which one.

At Borgo Egnazia, a luxury resort in Savelletri di Fasano designed as an authentic Puglian village, this awareness has become the subject of serious study and research. And so a hotel business, accustomed to the immediacy of service, has invested in something that stubbornly refuses to be rushed: seeds.

In spring and summer 2025, the Casa delle Sementi, or Seed House, recovered no fewer than 120 tomato varieties. Today, that collection has roughly doubled, and around 30 varieties have already made the journey from the vegetable garden to the kitchens of Domingo Schingaro, chef at the Michelin-starred restaurant Due Camini.

The Seed House is run by Angelo Giordano, an agronomist and seed saver who has spent years tracking down rare varieties in the countryside, scientific literature and networks of growers. Here, seeds are preserved, germinated and propagated, with the aim of bringing them back into cultivation and, once sufficient quantities can be produced, into the kitchen.

"I prefer to talk about varieties that have disappeared from the market rather than ancient varieties, because plants are living organisms. They continue to evolve. The tomato grown in Torre Canne a century ago, for example, has changed in the meantime. It hasn't remained frozen in time, waiting for us like some archaeological artefact."

His research focuses precisely on what the market has pushed to the margins, seeking to establish how much genetic, cultural and agricultural value remains hidden in those seeds.

Giordano arrived at Borgo Egnazia after spending years among what he describes, with a certain irony, as a community of "farming nerds": people who search for seeds where the market no longer looks.

The process begins in the countryside, searching for seeds, consulting archives and talking to elderly farmers. It involves reconstructing plant genealogies that often survive only in a family's memory. Then the network expands, and word of mouth begins to do its work. Today, around 30 growers are involved in the project.

"After a while," Giordano explains, "you find that they're the ones calling you because a plant has resurfaced in someone's vegetable garden, or because they've found a trace of a variety everyone thought had disappeared."

This is how the research gradually begins to turn into a genuine agricultural network.

Once Giordano finds a seed, his guiding principle is straightforward: it is worth preserving even if it initially seems unpromising. A particular variety may produce lower yields, be less convincing in terms of flavour or show certain limitations in the field. Yet it may still possess a valuable genetic trait. Natural resistance to a disease, for example, may emerge precisely when that disease becomes a problem for all the other crops.

In Borgo Egnazia's gardens, the research is conducted without synthetic chemicals and follows organic and regenerative farming practices.

Figures from the first documented growing cycle show four hectares under cultivation, with 200 endangered varieties planted, 322 recovered, 84 already propagated and 73 exchanged.

Angelo Giordano and Domingo Schingaro work almost like runners in a relay race, maintaining a dialogue that begins before the seeds are sown and continues all the way to the plate.

The agronomist must understand how a variety performs in the field and assess its potential for propagation. The chef tastes it, assesses its distinctive qualities and decides whether it has the potential to earn a place in the kitchen at Due Camini.

Sometimes the garden points the kitchen in a particular direction. At other times, Schingaro asks Giordano to investigate a variety further because it has revealed unexpected qualities. It is this constant back-and-forth between garden and kitchen that gives the project its most distinctive character.

Schingaro says his interest in vegetables grew out of a sense that something was missing in his own culinary background. "I realised there was a gap in my culinary knowledge. I hadn't paid enough attention to the whole world of vegetables because I'd never really had that produce in my hands." That realisation led him to study Puglia's biodiversity and begin working with Giordano.

Today, Due Camini is among the Michelin-starred restaurants that have opted for an entirely plant-based menu. After all, vegetables have always been at the heart of Puglian cuisine.

Tomatoes provide perhaps the clearest illustration of this approach.

The tomato fusilli on the summer menu incorporates seven or eight different varieties. Some are turned into sauce, others into sun-dried tomato purée, while others are fermented to produce a liquid extract. The pasta finishes cooking in that liquid, and the dish is completed with freshly grated raw tomato.

At that point, the tomato begins to demand recognition for its individual identity and origins.

And this raises perhaps the most interesting question of all: could restaurants eventually offer a tomato list, detailing each variety, its provenance and its culinary uses with the same care and attention currently devoted to wine?

For now, it remains a possibility. But the selection process is already under way, and the question is still on the table: if a sommelier can tell the story of a particular grape variety, why shouldn't we learn to do the same with a Tondino di Ginosa ?

items.title: Le classi popolari sono le vere protagoniste delle proteste francesi
items.summary: Il movimento per denunciare la situazione catastrofica della scuola, nato dal basso e lontano dall’antipolitica, rappresenta un punto di svolta nella politica francese e gioca in anticipo sui partiti Leggi
items.content:
Chiariamolo subito: il movimento studentesco che in questi giorni sta attraversando la Francia è impressionante. Le sue ripercussioni saranno numerose, e ovviamente incerte. Ma per la sua portata e la sua traiettoria, e per la sua polifonica irruzione nell’agenda politica, questa mobilitazione è già un punto di svolta della vita politica francese contemporanea.

L’importanza di quello che sta succedendo la si può misurare dall’incredibile levata di scudi delle forze reazionarie, che stanno tentando d’imporre l’immagine di un movimento con motivazioni dubbie, violento o strumentalizzato. Questo movimento mostra in modo clamoroso le irresponsabilità politiche del governo. I suoi avversari fanno bene a prenderlo sul serio.

In questa fase il movimento presenta alcuni tratti caratteristici e strutturali, che proverò a elencare ed esaminare attraverso una sociologia dei movimenti necessariamente ripensata alla luce di quello che sta succedendo. I punti che seguono non pretendono di essere esaustivi e devono essere letti come domande ancora aperte.

È la caratteristica primaria e ineludibile degli eventi di questi giorni: il movimento delle scuole superiori, ormai diffuso in tutto il paese, è nato negli istituti popolari della periferia parigina, nei dipartimenti di Seine-Saint-Denis e di Val-de-Marne. Al centro delle denunce di studenti e personale scolastico non c’è più la semplice “mancanza di risorse”, ma proprio il collasso degli istituti frequentati in gran parte da ragazze e ragazzi dei quartieri popolari.

Le prime richieste riguardano la parità di trattamento e sono formulate sulla base di una visione e di un’esperienza specifica delle disuguaglianze, rivendicando l’identità sociale dei quartieri popolari. L’estetica di questa mobilitazione, dalle parole al modo di vestire, si basa sui codici dei quartieri popolari. Rovesciando gli stigmi, il movimento testimonia la convergenza tra la cultura di strada e la presa di posizione politica.

Le immagini degli scontri tra studenti e forze dell’ordine hanno ricordato quelle delle rivolte dell’estate del 2023 . La continuità è evidente anche nel ruolo che fin dai primi giorni ha avuto la violenza della polizia. Il lancio a distanza ravvicinata di una granata contro un minorenne a Saint-Ouen-l’Aumône, ripreso in un video, e la vicenda di uno studente che a Tours ha perso un occhio sono già entrati nella storia della mobilitazione. In questo senso, il movimento degli studenti è erede delle recenti forme di protesta radicate nel mondo dei quartieri popolari francesi, e ne porta su di sé l’impronta culturale.

L’emergere dei ragazzi e delle ragazze delle classi popolari nel campo politico, attraverso questo movimento, si inserisce nel solco di una storia recente già molto dinamica: dalle manifestazioni spontanee dei giovani durante la crisi sanitaria del covid-19 all’esemplare mobilitazione elettorale contro l’estrema destra dell’estate del 2024, passando per le rivolte del 2023, in questi ultimi anni questi ragazzi stanno oggettivamente occupando il terreno politico, anche se queste aspirazioni democratiche sono costantemente negate o stigmatizzate.

Infine, questo movimento si inserisce in una guerra di posizione nella battaglia culturale contro l’estrema destra: molte figure pubbliche che rivendicano la vicinanza ai quartieri popolari stanno prendendo posizione, contribuendo ad alimentare un sistema culturale che fa emergere un’evidente linea di conflitto intorno alle questioni del razzismo e della democrazia. Considerati i loro riferimenti, i giovani manifestanti si inseriscono chiaramente in questo ordine culturale. Le elezioni presidenziali del 2027 influenzano questi posizionamenti. La scadenza elettorale non è identificata esclusivamente come una prospettiva, ma anche come un dato concreto e molto presente, che giustifica la mobilitazione e le conferisce rilevanza.

È un tratto distintivo della mobilitazione, forse non abbastanza evidenziato: i politici che si presentano alle manifestazioni sono trattati bene, talvolta perfino acclamati. E la tornata elettorale del 2027 è per lo più identificata come uno sbocco per la rabbia. Mentre da anni si parla diffusamente di una rottura tra ragazze, ragazzi e politica, e tra quartieri popolari e politica, queste proteste mandano un messaggio totalmente opposto.

I politici che arrivano con la fascia tricolore non sono accusati di “strumentalizzazione” dai manifestanti, ma sono accolti pragmaticamente come una preziosa fonte di sostegno utile ad amplificare la denuncia delle ingiustizie. Perché rifiutarlo? Fin dalla sua nascita la sollecitazione al mondo politico e alle istituzioni è parte integrante del movimento e delle sue rivendicazioni fondamentali. Le sue parole d’ordine non si collocano nel repertorio dell’antipolitica, ma si concentrano su richieste concrete: insegnanti, infermieri, ore di lezione, sedie, banchi.

Il movimento non si definisce contro le forme consolidate dell’impegno politico, né contro gli adulti (dal punto di vista della sociologia elettorale potrebbe senz’altro farlo) e si caratterizza per una forte solidarietà tra studenti e personale scolastico. La precarietà di quella che Pierre Bourdieu chiamava “la mano sinistra dello stato” si manifesta nella solidarietà a cui si assiste durante le manifestazioni, dove per esempio gli assistants d’éducation (figure che si occupano della supervisione e del monitoraggio degli studenti) stanno svolgendo un ruolo importante nella mobilitazione e nella legittimazione delle rivendicazioni di ragazze e ragazzi.

Il movimento è più in generale l’espressione lampante di una dinamica circolare tra culture popolari e cultura politica. Fin dalle prime ore della mobilitazione è apparso chiaro che la sua ascesa era indipendente da qualsiasi struttura politica consolidata. Partiti e sindacati non hanno alcun radicamento nelle scuole superiori ed erano “invisibili” nelle prime proteste. Questo non significa, sia chiaro, che la politica fosse assente. Infatti, le iniziative spontanee di documentazione delle condizioni scolastiche esistevano già sui social media, le varie generazioni si sono trasmesse l’esperienza della disuguaglianza.

Il movimento ha tra i suoi riferimenti i gilet gialli , di cui si riappropria con un discorso pubblico che sui social media dimostra un’evidente coscienza collettiva del contesto politico generale. I tanti interventi di studenti davanti alle scuole mostrano una notevole padronanza della comunicazione, che si rivolge alla società per parlare delle condizioni di vita sia negli istituti sia nei quartieri popolari. Il tema dell’ingiustizia, ben noto ai sociologi che si occupano dei quartieri popolari, è onnipresente e si lega a una richiesta di uguaglianza.

Come in molti processi di mobilitazione dal basso nel corso della storia, le difficili condizioni di vita sono state un acceleratore di politicizzazione ampiamente sottovalutato: si tratta di un tema che oggi sta entrando nel dibattito politico, ma che esiste da anni nelle contestazioni e nelle conversazioni quotidiane.

Qui sembra di notare l’emergere di una cultura politica alimentata dalle culture popolari più che dai tradizionali canali di politicizzazione. È senza dubbio questo l’aspetto che rende impossibile strumentalizzare il movimento: il suo essere espressione di qualcosa che è già lì, in anticipo sul mondo politico.

Ulysse Rabaté è un ricercatore in scienze politiche all’università Paris 8.

items.title: “In confronto a lei mi sento insignificante”
items.summary: Due giorni nella vita di due persone innamorate. Il primo, quando tutto comincia, e l’ultimo, quando ci si lascia. In questa puntata: Charlotte, 39 anni Leggi
items.content:
Due giorni nella vita di due persone innamorate. Il primo, quando tutto comincia, e l’ultimo, quando ci si lascia. A chi legge, la possibilità di immaginare cosa è successo in mezzo. In questa puntata: Charlotte, 39 anni.

Due settimane dopo la fine del mio contratto, sono invitata a una festa per celebrare le ultime pubblicazioni a cui ho partecipato. Mi vesto completamente di nero, scelgo scarpe con i tacchi e infilo al dito medio un anello tuareg di cui vado molto fiera perché è un pezzo unico, una specie di portafortuna. Per timidezza saluto rapidamente Zoé e mi dedico ad altre cose chiacchierando con gli altri, anche se continuo a tenerla d’occhio, attenta a ogni suo minimo movimento.

Mentre la festa è in pieno svolgimento, lei si dirige verso di me e con un sorriso travolgente mi porge una busta. ‘Aprila quando sarai tornata a casa’, sussurra prima di allontanarsi. Il cuore comincia a battermi all’impazzata, la vista mi si annebbia, le mani mi tremano. Ho la sensazione che quella busta contenga qualcosa di importante. Rispetto il suo desiderio e nel guardaroba infilo il biglietto nello zaino. Ho un unico desiderio: leggerlo.

Tornata a casa dei miei genitori, una volta chiusa la porta della mia stanza, apro la sua lettera scritta a mano. Una pagina fronte e retro, l’inchiostro blu, alcune parole dal tratto più marcato di altre, degli spazi che sembrano esitazioni. È una lettera piena di emozione che suona come una confessione: ‘Un solo essere vi manca, e tutto è spopolato’, conclude. Per la prima volta, sento la forza della celebre frase di Alphonse de Lamartine.

Aggrappata a quella lettera, che rileggo decine di volte, mi rendo conto che la nostra attrazione è reciproca. Mi infilo nel mio lettino, completamente sconvolta. Sarò capace di fare il grande passo con lei? Ho vent’anni e conosco poco l’amore, anzi pochissimo e soprattutto non smetto di ripetermi che è più facile amare gli uomini.

Ma l’indomani stesso, convinta di non poter farmi sfuggire questa storia, le do appuntamento in un caffè parigino, vicino a rue de Rivoli. Quando arrivo lei è già lì, sorridente, calma, osservatrice. Mi siedo, un po’ imbarazzata per quello che sto per dirle. Accendo una sigaretta e passo rapidamente alle confessioni. Mentre io immaginavo che ci saremmo baciate appassionatamente, lei resta interdetta, quasi scioccata dalla mia dichiarazione. ‘Non me lo aspettavo’, sorride. ‘Ti ho scritto per liberarmi dei miei sentimenti, senza pensare nemmeno per un secondo che tu potessi provare la stessa cosa’.

Mentre attraversiamo in silenzio la Cour Carrée del Louvre, mi prende la mano con fermezza e propone di andare a dormire in albergo. Quando ci presentiamo alla reception, a qualche isolato di distanza, sono molto orgogliosa di essere al suo fianco. ‘Due letti singoli?’, ci chiedono. Mi diverte correggerli: ‘Una camera matrimoniale’. Lei mi spoglia teneramente, ma io tengo addosso i miei slip di cotone Petit Bateau. Un modo probabilmente per non lasciarmi andare completamente.

Molto presto, dopo quella prima notte, lei lascia la sua compagna e va a vivere un po’ ovunque, da amici o in alberghi dove la raggiungo ogni sera. Ci amiamo appassionatamente e scopro i piaceri della carne. ‘Capitolo uno, capitolo due…’. Ogni notte mi impartisce con molta dedizione una piccola lezione di educazione sessuale. Ho l’impressione che mi stia insegnando a vivere la mia vita”.

Ha lasciato tutto per me: la sua compagna, il suo progetto di gravidanza, il suo appartamento. ‘Cosa ci fai con me?’, mi chiede, temendo che io prenda la nostra relazione un po’ troppo alla leggera. Chiaramente, non sono all’altezza delle sue aspettative. Ma mi è assolutamente impossibile prometterle un futuro insieme, nel momento in cui sento il bisogno di scoprire altri aspetti della mia vita sentimentale.

Un fine settimana, per parlarne più serenamente, mi porta nella sua casa di campagna dove facciamo delle sessioni fotografiche. Poso per lei tutto il giorno, nei campi, in un vecchio cantiere, sulla strada. Sono molto lusingata, ma al tempo stesso non capisco davvero cosa ci trovi in me. Non mi sento più molto a mio agio con me stessa da quando mi butto sul cibo a più non posso. È una cosa nervosa, mangio dolci di continuo. A fine giornata, invece di ritrovarci da sole a parlare del nostro futuro, beviamo qualcosa con due braccianti agricoli che ci provano con noi. Questo ci permette di non farci le vere domande.

Una volta tornate a Parigi ci vediamo sempre meno. Lei ha molto lavoro, è tornata per un periodo dalla sua ex compagna, non mi chiama più tutti i giorni. Soffro per questa separazione che ci sta consumando, ma non faccio nulla per riconquistarla. Mi concentro sui miei studi, sperando di incontrare presto un ragazzo per farmi un’idea.

Una sera la incrocio a una festa dove è venuta insieme alla sua ex compagna. Osservo la donna che aveva lasciato per me. Un portamento fiero, lunghi capelli neri ricci, una risata decisa, in confronto a lei mi sento insignificante. Noto che hanno una grande complicità. Io non valgo un granché rispetto a lei.

Qualche giorno dopo ricevo una busta di cartone. All’interno c’è un quaderno che contiene fotografie in bianco e nero di piccolo formato del nostro soggiorno in campagna. Tra una foto e l’altra ha scritto una favola per raccontare la nostra storia: io sono una piccola fata con tanti sogni e desideri. Scoprendo una pagina alla volta di questo quaderno a spirale, sono commossa da quest’ultimo regalo.

Quando arrivo alla terza di copertina, mi imbatto in una foto girata, attaccata alla buona con lo scotch. Una foto in più, come un post scriptum. Stacco l’adesivo e vedo Zoé, con il suo bel sorriso e i suoi occhi a mandorla. È di spalle, ma ha girato la testa, come per farmi un ultimo saluto. Se ne va per lasciarmi libera, senza rancore. ‘Ci lasciamo, ma è stato bello, no?’, sembra dirmi.

Più tardi, quando ho incontrato degli uomini, mi sono sempre sentita guidata da tutto ciò che mi aveva insegnato. Mi diceva di cercare la dolcezza degli uomini. Era convinta che avrei incontrato un uomo dolce”.

Amore che vieni, amore che vai è una serie del quotidiano francese Le Monde che racconta il primo e l’ultimo giorno di una storia d’amore. Qui ci sono tutte le puntate .

Internazionale pubblica ogni settimana una pagina di lettere. Ci piacerebbe sapere cosa pensi di questo articolo. Scrivici a: posta@internazionale.it

items.title: Samoa leader apologises for Nazi salute after video from 2007 emerges
items.summary: Schmidt acknowledged that his actions "were inappropriate and capable of causing offence and hurt".
items.content:
Samoa's prime minister has apologised after a video emerged of him giving a Nazi salute while saying "Heil Hitler" at a family gathering.

In the seven-second clip filmed in July 2007, Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Schmidt is seen leading about a dozen people in the salute. "Raise your right hand, Heil Hitler!" he says, then thanks the group for responding.

Schmidt has acknowledged that his words and gesture "were inappropriate and capable of causing offence and hurt", adding that the clip was recorded at a private gathering and "not intended for the public".

"I reject Nazism, antisemitism, racism and all forms of political extremism," Schmidt said in a statement published on Facebook on Monday.

The footage was first reported by local outlet the Samoa Observer in a news story on Sunday.

It said the video was filmed at a Schmidt family reunion in July 2007, when Schmidt was deputy speaker of parliament and quoted a family member who said he was the master of ceremonies at the gathering.

Samoa, a tiny island nation of about 221,000 people, sits about halfway between New Zealand and Hawaii.

It was under Germany's control in the early 20th century, but the colonisation ended shortly after World War One broke out.

Schmidt, who has Samoan and German heritage, took office as the country's eighth prime minister in September 2025.

He wore a Jewish prayer shawl during his swearing-in ceremony and has made clear his support for Israel during the early days of his premiership, saying that Samoa "stood with Israel".

"If people around the world don't like it, that's up to them, but Samoa stands with the land of God... There is only one God our country believes in, the God of Israel," he had said.

items.title: Fort Hood shooter to be executed by firing squad - a first for US military since World War Two
items.summary: Nidal Malik Hasan killed 13 unarmed soldiers and injured another 32 in the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.
items.content:
The Pentagon has announced it will execute a former US Army major by firing squad, the first such military execution in more than 60 years.

Nidal Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, injuring another 32.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell announced on social media on Monday that US defence secretary Pete Hegseth had made the recommendation and President Donald Trump approved it.

It will be the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War Two.

Parnell said the secretary of the US Army would set the time and place of the execution.

Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, killed 13 soldiers at the base in Texas in 2009 and later admitted in court he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes".

He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan.

The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.

The attack took place in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.

Watch: Why is America running out of execution drugs? , external

Hasan is currently one of four inmates on the US military's death row.

A military execution requires approval from the US president, according to military law.

It also requires appellate review and a final judgment on its legality to move forward.

The US Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces deemed the military death penalty unconstitutional in 1983 but it was reinstated the following year by an executive order under then-President Ronald Reagan.

Military executions differ from those carried out at the state level.

The majority of executions in the US are carried out on the state level, with 27 states, the military and the federal government still having capital punishment as a legally available option.

Death by firing squad is rather uncommon. There was an execution by firing squad carried out last year in South Carolina, a first for the state and the first time the method was used in the US in 15 years.

Four other states allow the use of a firing squad, including Idaho, Mississippi, Oklahoma and Utah.

Trump has been a proponent of the federal death penalty and re-instated it through an executive order on the first day of his administration in January 2025.

Under his predecessor, former President Joe Biden, the justice department had issued a moratorium on the federal use of the death penalty.

The executive order signed by Trump describes capital punishment as "an essential tool for deterring and punishing those who would commit the most heinous crimes and acts of lethal violence against American citizens".

US to allow firing squads, gas and electrocution for federal executions

items.title: Viaggio al centro della Terra: inizia in Valsesia
items.summary: Viaggio al centro della Terra: inizia in Valsesia
items.content:
Abbiamo fotografato gli anelli di Saturno, fatto atterrare rover su Marte e spedito sonde oltre i confini del sistema solare. Eppure il nostro pianeta resta in gran parte inesplorato proprio sotto i nostri piedi. Il pozzo più profondo mai scavato, quello della penisola di Kola, in Russia, si è fermato a circa 12 chilometri: appena lo 0,2% dei 6.371 chilometri che ci separano dal centro della Terra.
Per rendersi conto delle proporzioni, si può pensare a una mela. La crosta terrestre, con le sue montagne, gli oceani e le città, è sottile come la buccia. Sotto si estende il mantello, un enorme volume di roccia calda che scorre lentamente nell'arco di milioni di anni e che costituisce la parte più grande del pianeta.. Il Moho, la linea che nessuno ha mai toccato
Il confine tra crosta e mantello si chiama discontinuità di Mohorovičić, o più semplicemente Moho, dal nome del sismologo croato Andrija Mohorovičić che la individuò nel 1909. Studiando i terremoti nei Balcani, notò che a una certa profondità le onde sismiche improvvisamente acceleravano: segno che stavano attraversando un materiale diverso, più denso e rigido. Quella era la firma del mantello.
Da allora il Moho è diventato uno dei riferimenti fondamentali della geofisica, ma resta un confine "visto" solo indirettamente, attraverso le onde sismiche. Sotto gli oceani si trova a 5-10 chilometri di profondità, ma i fondali marini sono difficili e costosi da perforare. Sotto i continenti, invece, scende in media a 30-40 chilometri, e sotto le grandi catene montuose può superare i 60-70: una profondità impensabile per qualunque trivella oggi esistente.. La Valsesia fa eccezione
Ed è qui che entra in gioco un angolo di Piemonte. Chi conosce le Alpi tende a immaginare che, come in ogni catena montuosa, anche qui il Moho sia sepolto molto in profondità, sotto montagne che pesano e affondano nel mantello come un iceberg nell'acqua. In gran parte della catena è effettivamente così: sotto le Alpi occidentali la crosta si ispessisce e la Moho raggiunge anche i 50 chilometri e oltre.
Nella zona Ivrea-Verbano, però, la storia è diversa. Quando, decine di milioni di anni fa, la placca africana si scontrò con quella europea dando origine alle Alpi, un enorme frammento di crosta profonda e di mantello superiore fu spinto verso l'alto, fino a essere inclinato e portato vicino alla superficie.. Il risultato è un vero e proprio "spaccato" naturale della crosta: le rocce che normalmente si trovano a 20-30 chilometri di profondità affiorano oggi sulle nostre montagne, e le indagini geofisiche indicano che la Moho si trova qui a circa 2 chilometri sotto la superficie, contro i 30 e più della norma continentale.
In altre parole, non serve più scavare per decine di chilometri: in Valsesia la crosta profonda è già in superficie e il mantello è a portata di trivella. Non è un caso che in zona affiori la peridotite di Balmuccia, una roccia che proviene proprio dal mantello superiore ed è uno dei rari esempi al mondo visibili in superficie. Per questo l'area è considerata da decenni uno dei luoghi di riferimento per studiare l'intera sezione tra crosta e mantello.. Il progetto DIVE
Il sogno di perforare fino al mantello nasce negli anni Sessanta, con il celebre progetto americano Mohole, che puntava a bucare il fondale oceanico e fu abbandonato per difficoltà tecniche e costi. In pochissimi casi si è riusciti a scapito di sforzi enormi. Oggi la comunità scientifica internazionale ha individuato nella zona Ivrea-Verbano l'occasione migliore e l'ha messa al centro del progetto DIVE (Drilling the Ivrea-Verbano zonE).. Il pozzo di Vocca
Il percorso è stato lungo. Nel maggio 2017 un workshop dell'ICDP a Baveno concluse che quattro perforazioni tra Val Sesia e Val d'Ossola rappresentavano la strategia scientificamente più promettente. Seguirono i rilievi sul campo: nel 2020 due campagne sismiche congiunte, con GFZ Potsdam, Università di Losanna e Montanuniversität Leoben, indagarono la struttura profonda dell'area, compresa la zona di Balmuccia.
La prima fase, tra il 2022 e il 2024, ha riguardato la Val d'Ossola, con due pozzi a Ornavasso e Pieve Vergonte, profondi 579 e 910 metri. Non hanno raggiunto il mantello, ma hanno restituito campioni e dati preziosi sulla crosta continentale inferiore, mostrandone una variabilità inattesa. Ne sono nati numerosi studi, alcuni già pubblicati su riviste internazionali, altri ancora in corso.. Seconda fase: si scende in profondità
Il nuovo pozzo sorgerà nell'area di Vocca e dovrà scendere più del doppio dei pozzi ossolani, con l'obiettivo di raggiungere la passaggio tra crosta e mantello. Se l'impresa riuscirà, i ricercatori potranno finalmente analizzare la Moho direttamente: carotaggi di roccia, misure di temperatura, proprietà fisiche e fluidi.. Perché è importante toccare la Moho?
Capire com'è fatta e come funziona la zona di passaggio tra crosta e mantello aiuta a ricostruire l'evoluzione del pianeta, a comprendere come circolano i fluidi nella crosta e come si formano e si distribuiscono i giacimenti di minerali strategici, oggi sempre più importanti per la transizione energetica e tecnologica..

items.title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide
items.summary: US voters will head to the polls on 3 November in a ballot that could have a major impact on Donald Trump’s presidency.
items.content:
There are four weeks to go until the US midterm elections, when voters take part in a ballot that could have a major impact on the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.

On 3 November, Americans will choose members of Congress, which is made up of two parts - the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Elections take place every two years, and when they happen in the middle of the president's four-year term of office, they are called the midterms.

A key task of Congress is to create and pass federal laws - laws that apply nationwide.

The outcome of the midterms will decide which political party - Trump's Republicans or opposition Democrats - controls Congress and how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans.

The results are also seen as a measure of how happy people in the US are with the president's performance so far.

All 435 members of the House - the lower chamber of Congress - will be elected. They serve fixed terms of two years. The House is commonly where proposed laws are introduced and debated.

Meanwhile, 35 of 100 seats in the Senate, the upper chamber, will also be up for grabs. Senators serve six-year terms. Among other jobs, they approve or block proposed laws that have been received from the House.

On the same day, voters across much of the US will also choose state-level politicians. Governor contests in California, Florida, Georgia and Michigan will be among the most closely watched.

The US economy is on the minds of many voters struggling with the price of fuel, groceries, housing and healthcare.

Inflation remains above the level targeted by the US Federal Reserve, partly down to the war that the US and Israel started with Iran in February.

Democrats argue Trump's programme of trade tariffs has also pushed up prices for Americans.

Immigration is another key issue. Republicans say Trump has delivered on a major campaign pledge in 2024 by tightening the border and launching a widespread - and often controversial - crackdown on illegal immigration.

Concerns over AI have grown in urgency in recent weeks. Senior politicians from both parties have agreed on the need to regulate it - setting themselves in opposition to Trump, who has rejected the idea of laws to control development of the technology.

Congress is one of the three branches of government, alongside the presidency and the judiciary. Control of it matters for the shaping of legislation.

Both the House and Senate are currently held by the Republican Party. But its majority is a slender one. They have 218 seats in the House, which is the minimum number needed to control it, plus one independent who votes with them.

In the Senate, they have 53 seats. The upper chamber will only change hands if the Democrats win 51 seats, which would overcome a tie-breaking vote by the vice-president - currently a Republican - in the event of both sides getting 50.

If opposition Democrats win back control of at least one chamber, they will gain power to bring their own laws to the floor.

Voters have tended to "punish" the party of the president in the past and vote against them.

Recent polling shows a low approval rating for the president. He began his second term as president with an approval rating of just over 50%, according to polling resource website Silver Bulletin, but in early October it was sitting at about 37%. Meanwhile 61% disapproved of him.

But not all seats in each chamber are competitive. Some are a safe bet for Republicans or Democrats.

The BBC's US partner CBS News has identified nine Senate races to watch , external , in states like Iowa and New Hampshire, and 42 House races, in states like Arizona and Ohio.

The vote is more unpredictable this year because of a battle between the two parties over the way voting districts in the House of Representatives are drawn.

Republicans tried to gain an advantage by creating more favourable electoral maps in certain states and Democrats followed suit.

If the Democrats win either the House or the Senate then Trump will find it difficult to get any laws through Congress.

So his domestic plans could be frustrated, although he has found ways to exercise power without his wider party.

Democratic control of either chamber would also mean they could use committees to investigate aspects of the Trump presidency. Corruption allegations, the new White House ballroom and ICE tactics could be subject to scrutiny.

There is also a debate within the Democratic Party about whether to impeach Trump, which means to bring charges in Congress that will form the basis for a political, not criminal, trial.

If the Republican Party stays in control of Congress, Trump will be able to keep going with his plans for the remainder of his time in office.

The president's name is not on the ballot during the midterm elections, though Trump has urged Republicans to pretend that it is by voting for him as an endorsement of his actions so far.

Whichever way the results fall, commentators are likely to use them to make arguments about how voters feel about the direction of the country under Trump's leadership.

Trump cannot run to be president a third time. After the midterms, we can expect speculation to start building about who might be his successor as the Republican presidential nominee for 2028 - and who might compete against that person for the Democrats.

items.title: Example.com just launched the biggest redesign in decades
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.debugbear.com/blog/example-dot-com-redesign-history Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49971921 Points: 293 # Comments: 194
items.content:
example.com is a reserved domain name set aside by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) for documentation purposes. It has been available as an example URL for developers and writers since the late nineties.

While the overall messaging of the page has been consistent over time, the visual appearance has received several major overhauls.

In this article, we take a look at the recent changes as well as the evolution of example.com over the last 20+ years.

Until 28 September 2026, example.com was a static English-language page. The redesign introduces multi-language support using JavaScript, showing the content in a new language every 5 seconds.

Example.com shows an explanation of the site's purpose in English, Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish. This is the English-language message:

This domain is for use in documentation examples without needing permission. This is not a service, avoid relying on it for testing and monitoring purposes.

Along with introducing multi-language support, the JavaScript code also inserts an SVG book icon.

The new site doesn't just replace the content when showing the next language. Instead, there's a gradual opacity transition.

The opacity animation itself just uses transition: opacity .4s; . But how is the character-by-character transition implemented?

Each character is wrapped in its own span element, and each span gets a slightly larger CSS transition-delay than the one before it. That means each character's opacity animation happens at a slightly different time.

Example.com has now removed the animation and shows all languages right from the start:

IANA provided the following statement explaining the reasoning behind the recent changes:

The changes we make to the site from time-to-time are usually informed by a desire to either reduce the overall bandwidth demands of serving the site, or improve its utility. At its heart it is a placeholder for a site no-one should be accessing, but we have historically showed a message there to inform visitors about why the domain is registered and how they may use it.

As it tends to be heavily trafficked, the overall bandwidth is a key consideration, and to that end one of the changes we made this week was to split the page content into a more basic page, augmented by a separate Javascript file with additional content beyond that. Since most of the traffic to the site is automated it tends not to fetch the Javascript file, reducing overall data requirements.

The fundamental purpose of the domain is for use in documentation, such as illustrative examples you may find in instructions. We know that people may, for example, cut-and-paste a sample configuration file and forget to customize entries that contain an example domain, and we expect we get some incidental traffic from that. However, the domain isn't intended to be a general purpose endpoint for things like availability testing so we do not encourage that kind of usage. There is no requirement there is a HTTP service present on the host in order to fulfill its purpose, we just operate it as a courtesy.

According to Wikipedia , the example.com website launched on January 1, 1999. The earliest version available to view in the Wayback Machine is from January 20, 2002.

The earliest version of the website only featured a list of domain names reserved by the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) and IANA.

In the .com, .net, and .org top-level domains (TLDs), various domain names are reserved. These names are reserved from initial registration, but to the extent they are already registered the existing registrant may renew them.

Structurally, the HTML used a table layout, with the ICANN logo positioned in the top left corner of the page.

The server headers show that the site used Apache 1.3.22 at this point.

The first version of the example.com wording we recognize today came 67 days after the first available screenshot:

You have reached this web page by typing "example.com", "example.net", or "example.org" into your web browser.

These domain names are reserved for use in documentation and are not available for registration.

In February 2003, the content was amended to include a link to RFC 2606 , the official document for reserved top-level and second-level domains, so visitors could find more information on the website's purpose.

There was also a small technical change around this time: the server was upgraded to Apache 1.3.27 on Red Hat Linux.

The website then went unchanged for seven years. On July 30, 2010, a slight change was made: example.edu was now pointed to the landing page, alongside the three previous domains.

From January 2011, example.com didn't serve its own page. Instead, it redirected visitors to a page on IANA's website.

That changed on July 29, 2013, when the redirect was removed and example.com began serving its own page from the EdgeCast Content Delivery Network (CDN) instead of Apache, alongside a major redesign of the landing page. The new design used a rounded card with an reading 'Example Domain' and a new description of the website's purpose.

The viewable domain list was now gone, with a link to IANA's website for more information.

A new update came six years after the biggest change in the website's history. The layout remained the same, but the font stack was modernized to include more fallback fonts for devices such as Macs, iPhones, and Windows PCs.

The copy was tweaked slightly, with 'is for use in illustrative examples' replacing 'established to be used' and 'in literature' replacing 'in examples'.

Almost twelve years after the switch from Apache to the EdgeCast CDN, another infrastructure change took place: the Server header disappeared entirely. The response headers alone don't reveal which platform was serving the page at this point.

A change of provider around this time isn't surprising. EdgeCast had been acquired from Yahoo by Limelight Networks in 2022 and rebranded as Edgio. Edgio then filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in late 2024, with Akamai acquiring select Edgio customer contracts.

Later in 2025, the page was redesigned. The card design was dropped, and the HTML was minified. The copy was changed to a more direct message, again linking to IANA's website, with the link text changed from 'More information...' to 'Learn more'.

Less than a year after the previous switch, the infrastructure changed again: the site now serves from Cloudflare , as indicated by the cloudflare server header and CF-RAY header in the response. Whatever platform served the page after the January 2025 change, it has now been replaced with a Cloudflare-fronted setup.

The next update, on June 9, 2026, brought no visual changes. The only HTML changes on the page itself were a favicon tag being added and the tags being closed. The page now includes an empty favicon:

This avoids a lot of unnecessary requests, as otherwise browsers look for a favicon at /favicon.ico .

Example.com first introduced an "Avoid use in operations" message in 2025.

For developers, it's tempting to use example.com to check if the network is working or test HTTP requests. The example server likely receives a lot of traffic through this.

However, as the page now clarifies, it's not a service you can rely on. When we look at our uptime monitoring data, we can see that every now and then the example.com server doesn't respond correctly.

Using infrastructure that your organization controls can be more reliable.

Looking at the visual timeline, we can see that changes to example.com happen sporadically. Sometimes a couple of small tweaks happen in back-to-back months. Other times the website remains untouched for periods of up to seven years.

We have been monitoring the page for several years in our public demo project. The Chrome UX Report (CrUX) data shows how page speed has changed over time.

To learn more about how your website is performing, sign up for a free 14-day DebugBear trial.

items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia. Mar Nero, 3 navi colpite. Mosca: “Piani Nato portano a escalation”
items.summary: Massiccio attacco ucraino con 650 droni su Mosca: 2 morti. Dopo l’allarme degli 007 tedeschi, un piano Nato per gestire un'eventuale intrusione russa
items.content:
Due navi commerciali sono state colpite da droni nella zona economica esclusiva della Bulgaria nel Mar Nero. Un drone russo ha colpito uno dei ponti sul fiume Dnipro a Zaporizhzhia durante un attacco notturno. Per la prima volta dall'inizio della guerra, Kiev ha iniziato a installare reti protettive sui suoi ponti per difenderli dagli attacchi dei droni russi. Le barriere sono state montate lungo i lati del Ponte Nord, preso di mira negli ultimi giorni dalle incursioni russe. La misura, già adottata nelle aree del fronte nell'est e nel sud dell'Ucraina, serve a proteggere le vie di comunicazione dai piccoli droni esplosivi.

Cremlino: “I piani su basi Nato e armi nucleari in Lituania portano all'escalation”

Zelensky: “Abbiano notizie di intelligence su attacco russo su vasta scala”

L'ex capo del servizio di intelligence tedesco arrestato con l'accusa di spionaggio

Dall’Ue sostegno limitato all’agricoltura ucraina in caso di adesione

In caso di accesso all'Unione europea, l'Ucraina potrebbe vedere limitato il sostegno alla propria politica agricola e l'accesso al Mercato unico per i suoi prodotti agricoli. E' quanto si legge nel pacchetto di revisione delle politiche di allargamento, presentato oggi dalla Commissione europea. "Nel caso dell'Ucraina, date le dimensioni, la struttura e l'elevatissima produttività del suo settore agricolo, occorrerebbe prevedere disposizioni mirate per limitare significativamente il sostegno finanziario e l'accesso al mercato, aiutando al contempo l'Ucraina a recuperare l'accesso ai suoi tradizionali mercati di esportazione verso Paesi terzi", si legge in una nota dell'esecutivo europeo. La proposta, prevede un'integrazione graduale degli Stati candidati all'Ue, con un lavoro per approfondire l'integrazione in settori strategici quali l'energia, i trasporti, il digitale e la difesa. "Tale approccio integrerà e rafforzerà il processo di adesione, sviluppando la capacità amministrativa e la fiducia reciproca, pur rimanendo condizionato e reversibile. La Commissione avvierà dialoghi annuali con i partner dell'allargamento per monitorare i progressi, individuare opportunità e colmare le lacune nell'integrazione graduale", si legge ancora nella nota della Commissione europea. "Il settore agricolo ucraino è molto diverso in termini di produttività, costi unitari e sbocco internazionale in termini di vendite", ha spiegato un funzionario Ue. "Trattare questo settore come qualsiasi altro che affronta problemi di produttività e potrebbe aver bisogno di sostegno finanziario nell'Ue significherebbe confondere due situazioni oggettive molto diverse", ha precisato ancora motivando la proposta. Inoltre, ha concluso il funzionario, "se dovessimo reindirizzare queste esportazioni verso il mercato Ue, creeremmo seri problemi ai Paesi che attualmente acquistano, o acquistavano prima che la Russia iniziasse a bombardare le spedizioni di grano, grano e cereali ucraini", come i Paesi del Nord Africa. La proposta dell'esecutivo europeo viene incontro anche a vari timori espressi da alcuni Stati membri, secondo cui la produzione ucraina di cereali e semi oleosi potrebbe rappresentare un problema per il mercato Ue.

Ucraina, per la prima volta reti anti-droni sui ponti di Kiev

Per la prima volta dall'inizio della guerra, Kiev ha iniziato a installare reti protettive sui suoi ponti per difenderli dagli attacchi dei droni russi. Le barriere sono state montate lungo i lati del Ponte Nord, preso di mira negli ultimi giorni dalle incursioni russe. La misura, già adottata nelle aree del fronte nell'est e nel sud dell'Ucraina, serve a proteggere le vie di comunicazione dai piccoli droni esplosivi. Dall'inizio dell'invasione russa, nel febbraio 2022, le autorità temono attacchi contro le otto principali arterie stradali e ferroviarie della capitale, strategiche per la logistica della città. Le incursioni contro i ponti, iniziate la scorsa settimana, hanno provocato ripetute interruzioni del traffico e pesanti ingorghi a Kiev, che conta circa tre milioni di abitanti. Nei giorni scorsi il sindaco, Vitali Klitschko, ha avvertito che Kiev ormai deve prepararsi a una situazione di guerra, accusando la Russia di "fare a pezzi la città" con gli attacchi contro i ponti e le infrastrutture energetiche.

Mosca: “Un morto per peste negli Usa nel giugno scorso. In media 7 casi all'anno”

Una persona è morta di peste nel giugno scorso negli Usa. Lo afferma Rospotrebnadzor, l'agenzia federale russa per la salvaguardia della salute, dopo il caso sospetto di peste segnalato da media locali in Siberia, con la morte di una ricercatrice. "A giugno, nella contea di Santa Fe, in New Mexico, è stato registrato il primo caso mortale di peste del 2026", afferma l'agenzia russa in un comunicato, aggiungendo che, secondo l'agenzia per il controllo e la prevenzione delle malattie (Cdc) negli Stati Uniti "si registrano in media sette casi di peste all'anno, inclusi quelli mortali".

Domani compleanno di Putin, in agenda “una serie di telefonate internazionali”

Il presidente russo Vladimir Putin ha in agenda, in occasione del suo 74esimo compleanno domani, "una serie di telefonate internazionali". Lo ha dichiarato il portavoce del Cremlino Dmitry Peskov nel corso di un briefing con la stampa. "Il compleanno del presidente è raramente, per lui, una giornata dedicata esclusivamente ai festeggiamenti. Domani, ad esempio, è prevista una serie di telefonate internazionali, innanzitutto, com'è ovvio, proprio in occasione della ricorrenza. Vi terremo aggiornati", ha dichiarato Peskov ai giornalisti, come riporta la Tass.

Cremlino: “I piani su basi Nato e armi nucleari in Lituania portano all'escalation”

L'eventuale creazione di una base statunitense in Lituania e l'intenzione di Vilnius di revocare il divieto di dispiegamento di armi nucleari rappresentano un avvicinamento delle infrastrutture militari Nato ai confini della Russia e "un passo verso l'escalation delle tensioni". Lo ha dichiarato il portavoce presidenziale russo Dmitry Peskov, commentando i piani della Lituania di revocare il divieto di dispiegamento di armi nucleari sul proprio territorio e le valutazioni degli Usa in merito alla possibilità di creare una base militare permanente nel Paese baltico. "Se le infrastrutture militari di qualcuno, di un importante Paese della Nato, si avvicinano ai nostri confini, allora, ovviamente, questo non può che essere percepito come un passo verso l'escalation delle tensioni, proprio come il dispiegamento di armi nucleari sul territorio di uno Stato confinante", ha dichiarato Peskov, citato da Tass. "La Russia sarà costretta ad adottare tutte le misure necessarie per garantire la propria sicurezza", ha aggiunto il portavoce del Cremlino. Ieri, il presidente degli Stati Uniti, Donald Trump, non ha escluso la possibilità di stabilire una base militare statunitense nel Paese baltico.

Zelensky: “Abbiano notizie di intelligence su attacco russo su vasta scala”

I servizi segreti ucraini hanno ricevuto informazioni secondo cui i russi si starebbero preparando a sferrare un nuovo attacco su vasta scala. Lo afferma il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky. "Oggi abbiamo ricevuto informazioni aggiornate sui preparativi russi per un attacco su vasta scala. Stiamo preparando una contromisura", ha affermato, come riporta Rbc.

Rubio: “Spetta a Mosca dare prova di trasparenza sulla peste”

La Russia deve fare "maggiore chiarezza" dopo le notizie secondo cui un tecnico di laboratorio sarebbe morto di peste in Siberia. Lo ha affermato il segretario di Stato americano Marco Rubio, spiegando che Washington sta monitorando la situazione con estrema attenzione. "Ritengo che spetti ovviamente alla Russia condividere maggiori informazioni con il resto del mondo", ha dichiarato Rubio da Reykjavik, chiedendo a Mosca di dare prova di "trasparenza". Le dichiarazioni arrivano dopo che le autorità russe hanno smentito di aver adottato misure di contenimento contro la peste in seguito alla notizia della morte del tecnico, segnalata la scorsa settimana.

Mosca risponde a Trump: “Noi pronti ad aiutarvi nel controllo di epidemie”

La Russia è pronta ad aiutare Washington nel controllo delle epidemie di malattie infettive negli Stati Uniti. Ad affermarlo è l'agenzia russa per la salute pubblica Rospotrebnadzor, dopo che ieri il presidente degli Stati Uniti, Donald Trump si è detto disponibile ad aiutare la Russia in relazione a un presunto caso di peste. "La Russia è pronta a mettere a disposizione della parte americana specialisti, attrezzature di laboratorio, nonché strumenti per la diagnosi e la prevenzione", ha sottolineato l'agenzia sanitaria, citando in particolare alcuni recenti casi di malattie infettive verificatisi negli Stati Uniti, tra cui il morbillo e un caso mortale di peste.

Cremlino: “In Germania creano un nemico effimero per giustificare la militarizzazione”

"La creazione artificiale di un nemico effimero al fine di giustificare le spese per la militarizzazione" in Germania. Così il portavoce del Cremlino, Dmitry Perskov, ha definito oggi le dichiarazioni fatte ieri dal capo dell'intelligence tedesca, secondo cui la Germania rischia di essere coinvolta in un conflitto armato con la Russia, accusando al contempo Mosca di condurre una guerra occulta e attacchi ibridi. "Queste accuse sono assolutamente infondate e prive di qualsiasi base reale, le abbiamo già sentite più volte", ha affermato Peskov, citato dall'agenzia Interfax.

items.title: Friendship ended with Deno, now Node is my best friend
items.summary: Article URL: https://dbushell.com/2026/10/03/deno-to-node/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49971719 Points: 262 # Comments: 174
items.content:
I’ve been using Node heavily this month on a SvelteKit client project. When did Node get so good‽ Deno has been my go-to runtime for so long I forgot how to Node. Now I’m back, I find all the ECMAScript † sugar is supported and the old annoying APIs have been replaced or modernised. Most importantly, I never have to see require() .

† Doesn’t seem like that Oracle trademark dispute will see a positive end :(

The official Node docs recommend piping an internet script straight to bash (we never learn) to install NVM to manage Node & NPM. My (ancient) experience with NVM and NPM hasn’t been stellar. I heard Fast Node Manager (FNM) was better to switch Node versions. Obviously I roll bleeding-edge but I have client projects that demand stability.

I opted for PNPM too to avoid getting immediately pwned. (The “M” in NPM stands for “malware.”) Some scripts I use have hard-coded binary names ‡ , so I added two aliases:

‡ Edit: I might be confusing the time I symlinked various binaries. The aliases do help when copying steps from install guides that assume NPM is installed.

PNPM also blocks post-install scripts. Does NPM still yolo those?

I added additional settings to pnpm-workspace.yaml to delay malware updates.

At first I tried setting the minimum release age to “one month” because it takes Microsoft at least that long to remove reported malware. This caused dependency issues where PNPM struggled to match suitable versions. I settled for “one day”; long enough to allow some other sucker to beta test the next Shai‑Hulud.

Node can now run TypeScript without throwing a tantrum like a baby if the stars don’t align. That said, one does not simply publish TypeScript packages to NPM.

Why? Just strip the types bro, I know you can! Let me sign a deal with the devil!

To discourage package authors from publishing packages written in TypeScript, Node.js refuses to handle TypeScript files inside folders under a node_modules path.

This restriction is philosophical rather than technical. I get it though. TypeScript is a Microsoft product. Opening that floodgate would pollute the entire ecosystem. Nobody wants more Microsoft. I’d love to see light “native types” in ECMAScript. There are type annotation proposals . I suspect I’ll be retired before those bear fruit.

No TypeScript packages mean I need to find the latest churnware slop to bundle my stuff. Tsdown did the trick, with only two additional dotfiles. Not thrilled about that (every dotfile represents a mistake). I suppose I break even after deleting deno.json etc.

Speaking of Microsoft lock-in, because they wrecked GitHub I’m self-hosting my own Forgejo instance . NPM limitations mean my packages have lost “provenance”. I had to configure the PNPM trust policy to allow my own stuff. Fun times!

My final test for Node was converting my static site generator from Deno. Not many Node versions ago this would have required a major refactor. Today with Node v26.10.0 I found surprisingly little work to do.

The only required changes were to replace Deno’s file system API with node:fs — which is vastly improved from what I remember (literally ~10 years ago). Aside from that, I had to replace Deno.serve with Hono’s node adapter (a wrapper around node:http ).

After this minimum-viable migration I was shocked to see 15% faster builds . My codebase still favours idiomatic Deno. I bet I’m leaving performance on the table by not using other built-in Node APIs. That’s something to explore later. The only further change I made was to replace Deno’s @std/path with node:path which is a straight import swap.

So if I were to TL;DR in the middle: Node got a glow-up, wow!

You’ve probably known this for a while. I kept using Deno out of habit and familiarity. And I haven’t exactly been enthused to write server-side JavaScript recently.

I’m burying this part because it’s flogging a dead horse. Ultimately, Deno failed when they allowed the Silicon Valley Circus to define “success”. Deno went from an innovative modern JavaScript runtime to a boring start-up with uncompelling products . Half the employees were laid off and what’s left are tweeting AI fantasies and vibe-coding Temu Cloudflare.

There is no reason to use the Deno runtime today. Deno Land Inc. stopped innovating that years ago. Node has slowly but surely caught up, even surpassing Deno in places.

Basically stuff that made it borderline unusable on top of my other criticism. JSR support were very quick to delete my account on request. I don’t like leaving dead profiles around the internet. None of my packages are visible but old versions remain installable.
